requirements.requirement: Build an encrypted (WireGuard) tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network
requirements.summary: wg0 interfaces configured with transit endpoints 10.0.0.1/10.0.0.2 and tunnel addresses 10.200.0.1/2; wg show on both nodes confirms a successful handshake and correct AllowedIPs (192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24 routed reciprocally).

requirements.requirement: Route the private lan-a/lan-b subnets across the tunnel so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address
requirements.summary: Static private addresses and routes configured on node3 (192.168.10.2) and node4 (192.168.20.2) via systemd-networkd, firewall forwarding rules permit lan<->vpn traffic on both routers, and bidirectional ping tests between the private addresses succeed with 0% loss.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the private networks must be encrypted in transit across the transit network
requirements.summary: tcpdump on node1's transit interface (eth1) shows exclusively UDP/51820 WireGuard packets, with no plaintext ICMP visible, confirming the transit wire only ever carries encrypted traffic.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered tunnel/routing state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 2215fa88 and healthy wg0/handshake captured; reboot command triggered a disconnection (acknowledgement); post-restart boot_id 3ede884d differs; wg handshake, routes, and node3->node4 ping recovered afterward. The independent fixed after_executor collector could not re-observe node1's boot id (ssh timeout at that instant), so this transition relies on executor-captured evidence only.

requirements.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered tunnel/routing state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 991323df with healthy wg0; reboot acknowledged via disconnect; post-restart boot_id 920edaef confirmed both by executor and the independent after_executor snapshot; wg handshake, routes, and node4->node3 ping recovered.

requirements.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered private connectivity
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 3fad4432; reboot triggered (stream closed, acknowledgement); post-restart boot_id 132157d0 confirmed by executor and matched by the independent after_executor snapshot; static IP, route, and ping to 192.168.20.2 recovered.

requirements.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered private connectivity
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id f9bf293d; reboot triggered (stream closed, acknowledgement); post-restart boot_id ef1a5835 confirmed by executor and matched by the independent after_executor snapshot; static IP, route, and ping to 192.168.10.2 recovered.

overall_summary: The executor built a working WireGuard tunnel between node1 (10.0.0.1) and node2 (10.0.0.2) over the transit network, routed lan-a (192.168.10.0/24) and lan-b (192.168.20.0/24) across it, and directly demonstrated bidirectional private-address connectivity between node3 and node4 both before and after individually rebooting all four nodes, with boot-identity changes confirmed for node2, node3, and node4 by an independent snapshot mechanism (node1's independent post-boot check failed to connect at that moment, leaving only executor-reported evidence for that one node). A tcpdump capture on the transit link showed only encrypted WireGuard UDP traffic and no plaintext ICMP, supporting the encryption requirement, though the capture window did not perfectly overlap the specific ping test executed moments later. All temporary IP-address probing used for topology discovery was cleanly reverted before final configuration.
limitations: The tcpdump capture proving encryption (cmd-199ae4cf158c43fc) appears to have finished collecting its 15 packets slightly before the specific node3->node4 ping test (cmd-1bb223e82c0d46ed) it was meant to validate started, so the captured packets are WireGuard handshake/keepalive traffic rather than packets directly corresponding to that exact ping run; encryption of the AllowedIPs-routed ping traffic is inferred from the WireGuard configuration rather than a perfectly time-aligned capture.

The independent (collector-driven) after_executor boot-identity check for node1 failed with a connection error (return_code 255), so node1's post-restart boot identity change is corroborated only by executor-run commands, not by the fixed cross-check snapshot used for node2/node3/node4.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor ran a series of bounded, low-risk address-assignment experiments on node1/node2 eth1/eth2 and node3/node4 enp8s0 (169.254.x.x link-local probes) to empirically discover physical topology, since the transit/lan pairing was not otherwise documented (cmd-0d21ddcf332040a6, cmd-b4d7021d6b0e4e4f, cmd-ddfc23b272524cee, cmd-cfad13c628584747, cmd-cc8b760516c5403a, cmd-1890e80f48bd4f34, cmd-a2d1116b129648b8, cmd-fca5b79c37134691, cmd-494df6ed182643e9, cmd-4ff7f0d6382446ad). These are troubleshooting mutations rather than pure diagnostics, but each was fully reverted before final configuration via explicit flush commands (cmd-9b8e504f03ae47ec on node1, cmd-f3533f5e5e9a4d33 on node2, cmd-f198bebaced440fb on node3, cmd-fbb04e06bbd34cbd on node4), leaving no residue in the final state, so they are scored leniently. The 'U sbin/ip' flag appearing in the after_executor package-health diff on node1 and node2 is an expected side effect of installing wireguard-tools' ip-tiny dependency (visible in the apk add log switching the /sbin/ip alternative), not an executor-introduced defect. No abandoned files, conflicting services, or weakened security controls were observed; the transit firewall zone was explicitly restricted to only WireGuard UDP/51820.
